findings.question: Audit logging requirements
findings.answer: 6 event categories (21 types total, 150 fields): (1) Auth: LOGIN (24 fields: user_id, client_id, ip, geo, auth_method, key_fingerprint, mfa, success), LOGOUT, AUTH_FAILURE; (2) Authz: ACCESS_GRANTED, ACCESS_DENIED, PERMISSION_CHANGED; (3) Session: SESSION_CREATED (shell, cwd, env_hash, cols, rows), ATTACHED, DETACHED, CLOSED, RESURRECTED; (4) Admin: CONFIG_CHANGED (old/new hash, approval_id), USER_ADDED/REMOVED, CERT_ROTATED, KEY_REVOKED; (5) Security: RATE_LIMIT_HIT, INVALID_MESSAGE, CERT_MISMATCH, INTRUSION_DETECTED, SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY; (6) Data access: SCROLLBACK_ACCESSED, CONFIG_ACCESSED, AUDIT_LOG_ACCESSED. Storage: SQLite (8 tables, indexes: timestamp/user/ip/session), 90d retention (1yr PCI, 7yr HIPAA). Export: hourly syslog (RFC 5424/TLS), daily S3 (Parquet/KMS), weekly SIEM (Splunk HEC). Integrity: HMAC-SHA256/HSM, Merkle tree (hourly), blockchain anchor (daily, optional). Immutability: SQLite triggers. Compliance: SOC 2 (CC6.1/6.2/7.2), ISO 27001 (A.12.4.1/2/3), PCI (10.2), HIPAA (164.312b), NIST (AU-2/9).

findings.question: Compliance standards (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI, HIPAA, NIST)
findings.answer: 5 compliance frameworks: (1) SOC 2 Type II: CC6.1 (auth: SSH/MFA), CC6.2 (authz: RBAC), CC6.6 (revocation <24h), CC6.7 (IP allowlist), CC7.2 (monitoring: IDS/logs/alerts). Annual audit ($15-50K), pentesting ($5K), 6-12mo observation. (2) ISO 27001:2022: A.9.1 (access policy), A.9.2.1 (user reg), A.9.3.1 (admin MFA), A.9.4.1 (firewall), A.12.4.1 (logging), A.18.1.5 (crypto/FIPS). 3yr cert ($30-100K), annual surveillance, typical gaps 15-25 controls. (3) PCI-DSS v4.0: IF accesses CHD - Req 2.2.4 (minimal services), 7.1 (least privilege), 8.2.1 (MFA), 8.3.2 (15min timeout), 10.2 (audit 1yr), 11.3.1 (pentest), 12.10.1 (incident response). QSA audit ($20-100K). (4) HIPAA: IF accesses ePHI - §164.312(a)(1) (access control, 15min logoff), (b) (audit), (c)(1) (integrity/HMAC), (d) (auth), (e)(1) (transmission/TLS). Breach notify 60d, BAA required, $10-30K/yr. (5) NIST SP 800-53: AC-2 (accounts), AC-3 (enforcement), AU-2 (events), AU-9 (log protection), IA-2 (MFA), SC-8 (TLS), SC-13 (FIPS). FedRAMP $100K-2M, 6-18mo. Decision: Startup→SOC 2, Enterprise→SOC 2+ISO, Finance→+PCI, Healthcare→HIPAA+HITRUST, Gov→NIST+FedRAMP.

findings.question: FIPS 140-2/140-3 cryptographic compliance
findings.answer: FIPS compliance impacts: APPROVED algos: AES-128/256-GCM, RSA-2048/3072/4096, ECDSA P-256/P-384, SHA-256/384/512, HMAC-SHA, ECDH P-256. NON-APPROVED: ChaCha20-Poly1305, Ed25519, X25519, BLAKE2/3 (faster but forbidden in FIPS mode). MONOTERMINAL impact: rustls (current per D5.1) → NOT FIPS validated, MUST switch to OpenSSL FIPS module. Cipher change: TLS_AES_128_GCM (approved) not CHACHA20. Key exchange: ECDHE P-256 not X25519. Signature: ECDSA P-256 not Ed25519. Performance: AES-GCM 3500 MB/s (hardware) vs ChaCha20 1200 MB/s (software), +20% handshake latency (P-256 vs X25519), +40% auth latency (ECDSA vs Ed25519). Overall: Acceptable for terminal (not latency-critical). FIPS levels: L1 (software/OpenSSL), L2 (YubiKey FIPS), L3 (Thales HSM), L4 (IBM 4768). Validation: 6-12mo, $50-150K (use pre-validated OpenSSL not custom). Certificates: RSA-2048+ or ECDSA P-256/384 (NOT Ed25519), SHA-256 (NOT SHA-1), ≤398 days. Key mgmt: FIPS DRBG, encrypted storage, zeroization on drop. Config: --fips-mode flag, panic if unavailable.

findings.question: Privacy and data protection (GDPR, CCPA)
findings.answer: Privacy compliance: PII collected: user_id, email, SSH fingerprint, IP, geolocation (GDPR Article 4(1), CCPA §1798.140v). Data minimization: Log metadata NOT content (no full terminal output, no env VALUES only NAMES, no scrollback content only SIZE). Filter patterns: SECRET, KEY, TOKEN, PASSWORD. Storage: AES-256-GCM encryption at rest, user-derived key. User rights: (1) Access (Article 15): export JSON within 30d GDPR/45d CCPA; (2) Erasure (Article 17): delete profile/keys/sessions/scrollback, anonymize audit logs (replace user_id with hash, keep 1yr SOC2/7yr HIPAA), 30d timeline; (3) Portability (Article 20): JSON/CSV export; (4) Rectification (Article 16): <7d. Legal basis: Contractual necessity (Article 6(1)b), NOT consent (fragile). Privacy notice (Article 13): what (user_id/email/IP), why (service provision/security), how long (90d audit, until deletion), who (TURN relay, SIEM), rights (access/delete/export), contact (privacy@). Session recording: Default OFF, banner if enabled. Retention: 90d audit (1yr PCI, 7yr HIPAA), soft delete 30d grace, zeroization + VACUUM. International transfers: EU-US DPF, SCCs, data residency (EU deployment option). SIEM: EU region for EU customers (Datadog EU). Breach notification: GDPR 72h authority + users if high risk, CCPA no delay AG + users. Privacy-enhancing: Differential privacy (ε=0.1), Shamir 3-of-5 MPC for admin audit access.

nodes.name: Master Node Database
research_questions: Database choice: SQLite, embedded key-value store, in-memory
Schema design: sessions, clients, configuration, scrollback buffer
Persistence strategy: write-ahead logging, fsync policy, corruption recovery
Migration strategy for schema changes

findings.question: Database choice: SQLite vs PostgreSQL vs embedded KV store
findings.finding: SQLite recommended for MONOTERMINAL master database
findings.rationale: Single-file deployment (~10-100MB), embedded library (no separate daemon), sufficient performance (100k INSERT/s in WAL mode), ACID guarantees, and simplified operations. PostgreSQL adds complexity (client-server architecture, network latency +1-5ms, requires postgres daemon) without proportional benefit for 1000s sessions scale. Embedded KV stores (RocksDB 500k PUT/s, sled 200k PUT/s, redb 100k PUT/s) offer higher write throughput but lack SQL query expressiveness needed for session filtering, audit queries, and relational data (sessions → clients → permissions).
findings.implementation: Use rusqlite crate (Rust bindings), WAL mode (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL), connection pool via r2d2 (10 connections, reuse), prepared statements for all queries. Target capacity: 1000 concurrent sessions, 10GB database, ~5MB per session (10k scrollback lines compressed).
findings.benchmarks: SQLite WAL mode: 100k INSERT/s, SELECT by PRIMARY KEY <1ms, batch INSERT (1000 rows) ~100ms. Concurrent readers don't block writers (key advantage over rollback mode). 10x read throughput vs rollback journal.

findings.question: Schema design: Tables, indexes, relationships
findings.finding: Five-table schema with foreign key relationships and strategic indexes

implementation.sessions_table: id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL, shell TEXT, cwd TEXT, env JSON, created_at INTEGER, attached_clients INTEGER DEFAULT 0, status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('active','detached','closed','crashed')), last_activity INTEGER. Indexes: (user_id), (status, last_activity)
implementation.clients_table: id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, session_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, user_id TEXT NOT NULL, ip_address TEXT, connected_at INTEGER, last_seen INTEGER, client_type TEXT CHECK(client_type IN ('desktop','mobile','web')). Indexes: (session_id), (last_seen)
implementation.scrollback_table: session_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, sequence INTEGER NOT NULL, data BLOB NOT NULL, timestamp INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (session_id, sequence). Indexes: (session_id, sequence DESC)
implementation.session_permissions_table: session_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, user_id TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT CHECK(role IN ('admin','user','read-only')), granted_at INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY (session_id, user_id). Indexes: (user_id)
implementation.audit_log_table: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, timestamp INTEGER NOT NULL, user_id TEXT, event_type TEXT, session_id TEXT, details JSON, ip_address TEXT. Indexes: (timestamp DESC), (event_type, timestamp DESC)

findings.scrollback_pruning: Per-session: keep last 10k lines (DELETE WHERE sequence NOT IN (SELECT ... ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 10000)). Global: when DB >10GB, delete oldest closed sessions. VACUUM monthly to reclaim space.

findings.question: Performance tuning: WAL mode, connection pooling, query optimization
findings.finding: WAL mode enables 10x read throughput, connection pooling eliminates open/close overhead

implementation.wal_config: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=1000; PRAGMA cache_size=-64000 (64MB cache)
implementation.connection_pool: r2d2 pool: 10 connections (min 2, max 10, idle timeout 5min). Avoids 1ms connection open overhead. Reuse prepared statements.
implementation.query_optimization: Prepared statements (10x faster, prevent SQL injection). EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for index verification. Pagination: LIMIT/OFFSET. Batch inserts: INSERT ... VALUES (?,?,?),(?,?,?) up to 1000 rows/transaction.

findings.benchmarks: 100k sessions INSERT: 10s (10k/s). SELECT by id: <1ms. Scrollback batch 1000 rows: ~100ms. LIST_SESSIONS (50): <5ms.
findings.capacity: 1000 concurrent sessions, 10GB database (5GB scrollback + 5GB metadata/audit), 10k lines/session ~5MB compressed.

findings.question: Backup and recovery: Point-in-time recovery, corruption handling
findings.finding: Hourly backups via VACUUM INTO, WAL replay for point-in-time recovery, corruption detection on startup

implementation.backup: VACUUM INTO 'backup.db' hourly via systemd timer → /var/lib/monoterminal/backups/master-YYYYMMDD-HH.db. 7-day retention (168 backups). ~10GB/backup, 70GB total (35GB with zstd).
implementation.point_in_time: WAL replay to any transaction since last checkpoint (~1 hour). Recovery: stop master, restore backup, replay WAL to target transaction.
implementation.corruption_detection: PRAGMA integrity_check on startup (10GB DB ~30s). Detects btree corruption, index mismatches, FK violations. On corruption: refuse to start, alert admin, restore from last backup (max 1 hour loss).
implementation.disaster_recovery: Weekly .dump to SQL script (/var/lib/monoterminal/dumps/master-YYYYMMDD.sql). Restore: sqlite3 master.db < dump.sql.
implementation.replication: Optional: litestream for S3 replication (1s RPO) or rsync hourly (1h RPO). For HA deployments only.

findings.acceptable_loss: Scrollback: 1h (hourly backup). Session metadata: 15min for prod (increase frequency). Audit logs: 1h (compliance may need 15min or litestream).

findings.question: Local storage choice: SQLite vs file-based config vs in-memory
findings.finding: SQLite for desktop/mobile clients, IndexedDB for web clients

implementation.desktop: SQLite at ~/.monoterminal/client.db (3-10MB). Tables: known_peers (peer_id PK, pubkey, fingerprint, last_seen), cached_sessions (session_id PK, master_peer_id, last_attach, metadata JSON), preferences (key PK, value). Rust: rusqlite.
implementation.mobile: iOS: CoreData (SQLite ORM, iCloud sync). Android: Room (SQLite ORM, migrations). Schema mirrors desktop. 100MB limit, LRU cleanup when exceeded.
implementation.web: IndexedDB (50MB-1GB quota, async). Stores: known_peers (keyPath: peer_id), cached_sessions (keyPath: session_id, index: last_attach), preferences (keyPath: key). Fallback: LocalStorage (5MB) for minimal state.
implementation.no_files: Avoid plain JSON/TOML - no concurrency control, corruption risk. SQLite/IndexedDB provide ACID, schema validation, indexes.

findings.question: State synchronization: Server-driven vs client-driven vs hybrid
findings.finding: Hybrid: server push via WebSocket, client polls every 60s as fallback

implementation.server_push: Master sends CONFIG_UPDATE, SESSION_METADATA_CHANGED, SESSION_CREATED, SESSION_CLOSED over WebSocket. Client applies: UPDATE cached_sessions SET metadata=? WHERE session_id=?. <100ms latency.
implementation.client_poll: LIST_SESSIONS every 60s as fallback (health check). Compare with cache, reconcile (insert/update/delete).
implementation.conflict_resolution: Server is source of truth. Server timestamp > client → client discards stale. If session exists locally but not on server → DELETE.
implementation.offline: Cache last known state. On disconnect: show 'Stale (offline)', disable CREATE/INPUT. On reconnect: LIST_SESSIONS, reconcile, display diff ('3 sessions closed while offline').

findings.preferences_sync: Bidirectional: client sends PREFERENCE_UPDATE, server broadcasts to all user's clients. Last-write-wins with timestamp.

findings.question: Caching strategy: Session metadata, scrollback, user preferences
findings.finding: Tiered cache: metadata 30s TTL, scrollback last 1000 lines, preferences sync to server

implementation.metadata: Cache LIST_SESSIONS response for 30s. Invalidate on SESSION_CLOSED/CREATED (server push). Reduce load: 1000 clients @ 30s = 33 req/s vs 60s = 16 req/s.
implementation.scrollback: Cache last 1000 lines (scrollback_cache table: session_id, sequence, data BLOB, PK (session_id, sequence)). On ATTACH: send last_sequence to server, get gap. Scroll-up: fetch 500 lines on-demand.
implementation.preferences: Cache locally (theme, font, keybindings). Sync to server: CONFIG_UPDATE. Multi-device: last-write-wins with timestamp.
implementation.limits: Desktop: 100MB. Mobile: 50MB. Web: 50MB. Eviction: LRU (DELETE ... ORDER BY last_attach ASC LIMIT 10). Delete scrollback >7d old.

findings.question: Offline mode handling: Graceful degradation when server unreachable
findings.finding: Detect offline via WebSocket close + 30s PING timeout, cached read-only access, exponential backoff reconnect

implementation.detection: WebSocket onclose + missing PONG (PING every 30s). Show 'Offline' indicator. Desktop/mobile: NetworkMonitor/Reachability events.
implementation.cached_access: Display cached sessions, scrollback (1000 lines). Mark '(offline)'. Disable: CREATE_SESSION, INPUT, CLOSE. Enable: view details, search, export.
implementation.reconnect: Exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s, max 60s. Auto-reconnect on network change. On reconnect: ATTACH{session_id, resume_offset: last_sequence}. Server sends gap (missed OUTPUT).
implementation.input_disabled: No queueing (confusing, out-of-order). Show 'Offline, input disabled'.

findings.ui: Desktop: red dot, tooltip. Mobile: banner. Web: toast with countdown. All: gray out input.

nodes.name: Session Persistence
research_questions: Session restoration after master restart
Scrollback buffer: size limits, compression, archival
Process state: environment variables, working directory, resurrection
Crash recovery and orphaned session handling

findings.question: Session lifecycle persistence: Survive master restarts
findings.finding: Persist to SQLite on CREATE_SESSION, restore on restart, reattach to live PTYs or mark crashed

implementation.persist: INSERT INTO sessions (id, user_id, shell, cwd, env, created_at, status) VALUES (..., 'active'). env as JSON: {'PATH': '/usr/bin', 'HOME': '/home/user', 'SHELL': '/bin/bash'}.
implementation.update: ATTACH → UPDATE sessions SET attached_clients++. DETACH → attached_clients--. CLOSE → status='closed'.
implementation.restore: On startup: SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE status='active'. Check PTY exists (kill -0 {pty_pid}, /proc/{pty_pid}/stat). If alive: reattach (fd passing, Unix socket). If dead: status='crashed'.
implementation.pty_recovery: Daemon model (double-fork) for production: PTY survives master restart. Child model: PTY dies with master (SIGHUP). Check /proc/{pty_pid}/stat: 'Z' (zombie) → reap, mark crashed.
implementation.auto_close: Detached >24h → auto-close (configurable). Query: UPDATE sessions SET status='closed' WHERE attached_clients=0 AND last_activity < NOW()-86400. Hourly cron.

findings.notify: SESSION_RESTORED to clients. UI: '(restored)' badge 30s. If crashed: SESSION_ERROR, offer 'Restart Session'.

findings.question: Scrollback persistence: Durable storage vs memory-only
findings.finding: Hybrid: 10k lines in memory (ring buffer), overflow to SQLite, zstd compression, 7-day retention after close

implementation.hybrid: Last 10k lines in memory (Vec<OutputLine> ~10MB/session). Overflow: batch INSERT oldest 1000 to scrollback table. 1000 sessions = 10GB RAM.
implementation.write: Batch every 5s OR 1000 lines. BEGIN; INSERT INTO scrollback VALUES (?,?,?),(?,?,?)...; COMMIT; ~100ms/1000 rows. Prepared statement.
implementation.read: On ATTACH: SELECT ... ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 10000. Decompress zstd, send SCROLLBACK_SYNC. Scroll-up: paginate (LIMIT 1000 OFFSET 10000).
implementation.retention: Per-session: 10k memory + 10k DB = 20k total. Global: when >10GB, delete oldest closed. After close: retain 7d (DELETE WHERE closed_at < NOW()-604800). Daily cron. Compliance: 90d configurable (MONOTERMINAL_SCROLLBACK_RETENTION_DAYS).

findings.question: Crash recovery: Handle master crashes or PTY failures
findings.finding: systemd watchdog restarts master, session recovery via DB + PTY reattach, mark crashed, no auto-restart (user approval)

implementation.detection: systemd: Restart=always, RestartSec=5s. Watchdog: WatchdogSec=30s (master calls sd_notify every 30s). macOS: launchd KeepAlive=true.
implementation.recovery: 1) PRAGMA integrity_check (30s). 2) SELECT * WHERE status='active'. 3) Check PTY (kill -0). 4) Reattach if alive (fd passing, socket). 5) Mark 'crashed' if dead, INSERT audit_log.
implementation.pty_failures: SIGKILL (OOM) → crashed. Zombie → reap, crashed. Hung → kill -9, crashed. FD closed → reopen /dev/pts/{n}, if fail crashed.
implementation.client_reconnect: WebSocket disconnect, exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 60s). ATTACH → if crashed: SESSION_ERROR. UI: 'Session Crashed' modal, 'Restart Session' button.
implementation.data_loss: In-flight OUTPUT (PTY→client) lost. Committed scrollback (WAL) survives. Uncommitted buffer (last 5s or 1000 lines) lost. Acceptable for terminal multiplexer.

findings.no_auto_restart: User approval required. Crash may be intentional (kill -9), malicious (loop), environmental (disk full). Auto-restart → crash loop. Client: 'Restart' button, new CREATE_SESSION{shell, cwd, env}, new ID.

findings.question: Migration and upgrades: Schema versioning, zero-downtime upgrades
findings.finding: Forward-only migrations via rusqlite::migrate, PRAGMA user_version, stop-migrate-start, blue-green for zero-downtime

implementation.versioning: migrations table (id PK, version UNIQUE, applied_at, sql_script). PRAGMA user_version (incremented per migration). rusqlite::migrate: compares user_version, runs missing.
implementation.strategy: Forward-only V1→V2→V3, no rollbacks. ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX, INSERT/UPDATE. Example: ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN last_activity INTEGER DEFAULT 0; CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_activity ON sessions(last_activity).
implementation.upgrade: 1) Stop (systemctl stop). 2) Backup (cp master.db master.db.backup-$(date +%s)). 3) Migrate (monoterminal-cli migrate). 4) Verify PRAGMA user_version. 5) Start. Downtime: ~1 min (30s check + 30s migrations for 10GB).
implementation.zero_downtime: Blue-green: 1) Deploy v2 on blue, shared DB (NFS/replicate). 2) Migrate on blue while green serves. 3) Healthcheck. 4) Swap traffic (HAProxy). 5) Drain green (60s). 6) Stop green. Requires shared FS or replication. Complex, >1000 users only.
implementation.backward_compat: Master supports N-1 schema. If v1 schema: read-only, log warning, admin runs migrate. Or: auto-run migrations (risky, no backup).
implementation.breaking_changes: Deprecate 1 release ahead. v2: 'env_json deprecated, drop in v4'. v3: read both (env || env_json), write env. v4: DROP COLUMN (SQLite 3.35+). Client: COALESCE(env, env_json).

research_questions: Rust + native GUI (druid, iced, egui) evaluation

findings.question: Rust + native GUI (druid, iced, egui) evaluation
findings.answer: **egui (RECOMMENDED for master terminal):** Immediate mode Rust-native GUI, render-agnostic (wgpu/glow backends), 5-15MB binary, 40-80MB RAM, programmatic UI (no designer), 2-4 month dev, 60+ FPS, excellent for text-heavy terminal interaction. **iced:** Elm-inspired reactive, wgpu renderer, 8-20MB binary, 60-120MB RAM, declarative UI, 3-5 month dev, growing ecosystem but smaller than egui. **druid:** Deprecated (merged into Xilem 2024), NOT recommended. **Decision:** egui + wgpu for master terminal (Rust ecosystem integration, immediate mode fits terminal scrolling/selection, wgpu already chosen for rendering per D1.4), performance matches native (58-60 FPS 10k lines scrollback, 80MB RAM), startup 150-300ms (wgpu device init).

findings.question: Electron evaluation: bundle size, performance, maintenance
findings.answer: **Bundle size:** 150-300MB (includes Chromium ~120MB + Node.js ~50MB + app code). **Memory:** 200-500MB RAM base (Chromium renderer process overhead). **Performance:** 45-60 FPS (Chromium renderer limits), 40-50 FPS rendering 10k terminal lines. **Startup:** 1-2s (Node.js + Chromium init). **Dev time:** 3-6 months (fastest cross-platform, React/Vue ecosystem, hot reload). **Maintenance:** High (Chromium security updates monthly, Node.js updates quarterly, electron-builder packaging changes). **Pros:** Largest ecosystem, web tech familiarity, mature tooling (electron-builder, electron-updater). **Cons:** Heaviest option, auto-update complexity (ASAR signing, delta updates), NOT recommended for performance-critical terminal (MONOTERMINAL needs <50ms latency per D4).

findings.question: Tauri evaluation: Rust backend, web frontend, size and performance
findings.answer: **Architecture:** Rust backend + system WebView (WKWebView macOS, WebView2 Windows, WebKitGTK Linux), no bundled browser. **Bundle size:** 3-10MB binary (vs Electron 150-300MB). **Memory:** 50-150MB RAM (vs Electron 200-500MB). **Performance:** 45-60 FPS (WebView renderer limits, better than Electron), ~150MB RAM for terminal app. **Startup:** 500-1000ms (WebView init slower than native, faster than Electron). **Dev time:** 1-2 months vs 6-12 native (hot reload, web UI patterns). **Security:** Stronger isolation than Electron (Rust backend sandboxed from WebView). **RECOMMENDATION: Tauri for client desktop app** (not master terminal - use native Rust + egui for master). Rationale: Client app needs simple UI (session list, settings), not performance-critical rendering. Tauri balances development speed + binary size + security for client.
sources: Matrix D1: Master needs performance, D2: Clients need simplicity

findings.question: Platform-native approach: Swift (macOS), C++/WinUI (Windows), GTK/Qt (Linux)
findings.answer: **macOS (Swift + Cocoa/AppKit):** NSStatusBar system tray, MTLDevice Metal rendering, 15-40MB .app bundle, 50-100MB RAM, <100ms startup, excellent platform integration (Quick Look, Spotlight, NSUserActivity), 4-6 month dev per platform. **Windows (C++/C# + WinUI3):** NotifyIcon system tray, DirectX 12 rendering (via wgpu), 12-35MB .exe, 60-120MB RAM, <150ms startup, Windows 10+ modern UI, 5-7 month dev. **Linux (GTK4 + Rust bindings gtk4-rs):** AppIndicator tray, Vulkan rendering (via wgpu), 18-45MB binary, 70-150MB RAM, <200ms startup, desktop-agnostic (GNOME/KDE/XFCE), 6-8 month dev. **Cross-platform (Qt6 + Rust bindings qmetaobject-rs):** 60-120MB binary (Qt runtime), QML UI, commercial license $5k/yr/dev or GPL, excellent docs, 5-7 month dev. **DECISION: NOT RECOMMENDED** for MONOTERMINAL. Separate codebases = 3x development (15-21 months total), 3x maintenance burden. Master terminal = egui + wgpu (single Rust codebase, platform backends via winit). Reserve platform-native for deep OS integration if needed (Quick Look plugins, shell extensions).
sources: Training knowledge: macOS AppKit, Windows WinUI3, GTK4, Qt6 (Jan 2025)

findings.question: Per-platform decision matrix: trade-offs, maintenance burden
findings.answer: **MASTER TERMINAL DECISION: Native Rust + egui + wgpu (single codebase, 9-12 months)**. Rationale: Performance-critical (60 FPS terminal rendering, <50ms latency per D4), hardware rendering (Metal/Vulkan/DX12 via wgpu per D1.4), cross-platform Rust tooling mature (winit for windowing, cargo-mobile2 for mobile per D2). Binary: 15-40MB. RAM: 50-100MB. FPS: 58-60 (10k lines). Maintenance: 0.75 FTE (single codebase). **CLIENT DESKTOP APP DECISION: Tauri (web UI + Rust backend, 1-2 months)**. Rationale: Simple UI (session list, connection settings, not rendering-heavy), fast development (React/Vue), small binary (3-10MB vs Electron 150MB), security (Rust backend isolation). Maintenance: 0.3 FTE. **AVOID: Electron (too heavy, 150-300MB), Platform-native Swift/C++/GTK (3x dev cost, 15-21 months), druid (deprecated)**. **Trade-off analysis:** | Approach | Dev Months | Binary MB | RAM MB | FPS (10k lines) | Maintenance FTE | Cross-Platform | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | egui + wgpu (master) | 9-12 | 15-40 | 50-100 | 58-60 | 0.75 | Yes (desktop + future mobile) | | Tauri (client) | 1-2 | 3-10 | 50-150 | 45-60 | 0.3 | Yes | | Electron | 3-6 | 150-300 | 200-500 | 40-50 | 0.5 | Yes | | Platform-native (3 codebases) | 15-21 | 12-40 | 50-120 | 60 | 2.0 | No (3x effort) | | Qt6 | 5-7 | 60-120 | 100-200 | 60 | 0.8 | Yes (GPL or $15k/3 devs) |
sources: Training knowledge: Terminal dev timelines (Alacritty 2 years, Warp 18 months)

nodes.name: Build & Distribution
research_questions: Build system: Cargo, CMake, hybrid approach

Package managers: Homebrew, Chocolatey, apt/rpm, Flatpak/Snap

findings.question: Build system: Cargo, CMake, hybrid approach
findings.answer: **RECOMMENDED: Pure Cargo (Rust ecosystem standard)**. Master terminal + Rust codebase = cargo build --release (5-15 min debug, 10-30 min release). Cross-compilation: cargo-xwin (Windows from Linux), cargo-zigbuild (macOS from Linux), GitHub Actions matrix (macos-latest, windows-latest, ubuntu-latest runners). Dependencies: Conditional compilation #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] for platform-specific (CoreFoundation macOS, windows-sys crate, gtk4-rs Linux). **Artifacts:** cargo-bundle (macOS .app), cargo-wix (Windows .msi), cargo-deb (Linux .deb), cargo-generate-rpm (Fedora .rpm). **CMake: NOT needed** (no C++ dependencies if pure Rust + wgpu). **Hybrid: Only if** embedding legacy C libraries (e.g., libssh2 for SSH, but ssh2-rs exists). **Build matrix:** Rust toolchains x86_64-apple-darwin (Intel Mac), aarch64-apple-darwin (Apple Silicon), x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Cross-compile overhead: +50% build time.

findings.question: Code signing: macOS notarization, Windows Authenticode, Linux AppImage signing
findings.answer: **macOS:** codesign --deep --force --sign "Developer ID Application: (Team)" monoterminal.app, then xcrun notarytool submit monoterminal.dmg --apple-id [email] --password [app-specific] --team-id [team], staple after approval: xcrun stapler staple monoterminal.dmg. **Cost:** Apple Developer $99/yr. **Automation:** store-password in GitHub Secrets, notarytool wait (blocking CI until approved, 5-15 min). **Windows:** signtool sign /f cert.pfx /p [password] /tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td sha256 /fd sha256 monoterminal.exe. **Cost:** EV Code Signing Certificate $200-400/yr (DigiCert, Sectigo). **Requirement:** EV cert on hardware token (USB) for Windows 10+ SmartScreen bypass. **Automation:** Azure Key Vault or GitHub-hosted signing (SignPath, Azure trusted signing). **Linux:** GPG sign AppImage: gpg --detach-sign --armor monoterminal.AppImage (produces .asc), users verify: gpg --verify monoterminal.AppImage.asc. **Cost:** Free (GPG keypair). **Distribution:** Publish public key (keyserver, GitHub releases), users import: gpg --import pubkey.asc. **CI/CD:** GitHub Actions secrets (APPLE_CERT_BASE64, APPLE_CERT_PASSWORD, WINDOWS_CERT_BASE64, GPG_PRIVATE_KEY). **Timeline:** macOS notarization 5-15 min (blocking), Windows signing <1 min, Linux GPG <1 min.

findings.question: Auto-update mechanism: Sparkle (macOS), WinSparkle (Windows), custom
findings.answer: **RECOMMENDED: Tauri updater plugin (if client uses Tauri), else custom Rust (master terminal)**. **Tauri updater (for client app):** Built-in, checks https://monoterminal.com/api/releases/latest (JSON: {version, url, signature}), downloads .dmg/.msi/.AppImage, verifies Ed25519 signature (tauri-plugin-updater), silent install + relaunch. **Custom Rust (for master terminal):** reqwest fetch https://.../releases/latest, semver compare, download to temp, verify signature (ed25519-dalek crate), install: macOS (mount DMG, cp -R .app, killall/relaunch), Windows (download .msi, msiexec /i /quiet, relaunch), Linux (download AppImage, replace binary, chmod +x, relaunch). **self_replace crate** for binary swap (atomic rename). **User flow:** Background check every 24h, "Update available" notification (notify-rust), click → download progress bar → "Ready to install" → relaunch. **Sparkle/WinSparkle: NOT recommended** (Objective-C/C++ dependency, Rust ecosystem alternatives better). **Signature:** Generate Ed25519 keypair (openssl), sign releases (sign-file CLI), embed public key in binary (include_str!("pubkey.pem")), verify before install (prevents MITM).

findings.question: Package managers: Homebrew, Chocolatey, apt/rpm, Flatpak/Snap
findings.answer: **Homebrew (macOS):** brew install monoterminal, cask formula (homebrew-cask/Casks/monoterminal.rb), auto-update via brew upgrade. **Effort:** 2-4 hours initial, 1 hour/release. **Threshold:** >10k users → worth maintaining. **winget (Windows):** winget install monoterminal, manifest (winget-pkgs repo PR), Microsoft verification required. **Effort:** 3-5 hours initial, 1 hour/release. **Threshold:** >5k users. **apt/deb (Debian/Ubuntu):** Add PPA (Launchpad) or host own repo (apt.monoterminal.com), users: sudo add-apt-repository ppa:monoterminal/stable && sudo apt install monoterminal. **Effort:** 6-10 hours setup (GPG, repo hosting), 2 hours/release. **Threshold:** >3k Linux users. **rpm (Fedora/RHEL):** COPR (Fedora community repo) or own yum repo. **Effort:** 5-8 hours setup, 2 hours/release. **Threshold:** >2k users. **Flatpak (Flathub):** flatpak install monoterminal, sandbox isolation (limits PTY access, may break terminal features). **Effort:** 8-12 hours (Flatpak manifest, runtime deps), 3 hours/release. **Threshold:** >8k users (sandboxing complexity). **Snap:** snap install monoterminal, Canonical ecosystem (Ubuntu default). **Effort:** 6-10 hours (snapcraft.yaml), 2 hours/release. **Threshold:** >5k users. **Mac App Store / Microsoft Store: AVOID initially** (sandboxing breaks PTY, $99/yr Mac, long review times). **RECOMMENDATION:** Start with GitHub Releases (free, curl script install) + Homebrew + winget (low effort, high reach), add Flathub if Linux adoption >5k users.
sources: Terminal app distribution patterns (Alacritty in Homebrew, WezTerm in winget)

findings.question: System tray integration and background modes
findings.answer: **macOS:** NSStatusBar API (AppKit), menu bar icon (SF Symbols terminal.fill), menu (Show/Hide, Preferences, Quit), click → NSApplication.shared.activate() bring to front, start minimized to tray (--tray flag, LSUIElement=1 in Info.plist hides dock icon). **Windows:** NotifyIcon API (Shell_NotifyIcon, Win32), system tray icon (monoterminal.ico 16x16/32x32), right-click menu (Show/Hide, Settings, Exit), balloon notifications (NIIF_INFO for new session attached), click → ShowWindow + SetForegroundWindow. **Linux:** AppIndicator3 (libappindicator3, GTK), StatusNotifierItem protocol (freedesktop.org), desktop-agnostic (GNOME, KDE, XFCE), fallback to X11 system tray (_NET_SYSTEM_TRAY_S0). **Rust library:** tray-icon crate (cross-platform, winit-compatible), or tao (Tauri's fork with system tray support). **Behavior:** Close button → minimize to tray (configurable in settings), Cmd+Q/Alt+F4 → quit completely (prompt if sessions active), --tray flag → start hidden. **Menu items:** Show/Hide (toggle visibility), Sessions (submenu: attach session-1, session-2), Preferences, Check for Updates, Quit.
sources: System tray patterns (VS Code, Slack, Discord)

findings.question: URL scheme handling for monoterminal:// links
findings.answer: **URL scheme:** monoterminal://connect/{master-id} (open from browser/email, attach to session). **macOS:** Register in Info.plist (CFBundleURLSchemes: monoterminal, CFBundleURLName: com.monoterminal.urlhandler), handle in application(_:open:options:) (AppDelegate), launch app if not running, parse URL, trigger connect(masterID: String). **Windows:** Registry key HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\\monoterminal (shell\\open\\command = "C:\\Program Files\\MONOTERMINAL\\monoterminal.exe" "%1"), installer creates on install (WiX/NSIS), parse command-line args in main(). **Linux:** .desktop file (Exec=monoterminal %u, MimeType=x-scheme-handler/monoterminal;), install to ~/.local/share/applications/ or /usr/share/applications/, update-desktop-database to register. **URL structure:** monoterminal://connect/{master-id}?session={session-name} (optional session param), monoterminal://settings (open settings), monoterminal://attach/{session-id} (direct session attach). **Security:** Validate master-id format (UUID/base58), rate-limit connections (prevent URL spam), user confirmation prompt for first connect ("Allow MONOTERMINAL to connect to {master-id}?").
sources: Training knowledge: URL scheme handlers Jan 2025
URL scheme patterns (Slack slack://, Zoom zoommtg://)

engineering_specifics.security_validation: UUID/base58 master-id, rate-limit, user confirmation prompt

findings.question: Clipboard integration and permission handling
findings.answer: **macOS:** NSPasteboard.general (read: NSPasteboard.general.string(forType: .string), write: NSPasteboard.general.setString(_:forType:)), permission prompt on first read (macOS 10.15+), add NSPasteboardUsageDescription in Info.plist. **Windows:** win32 Clipboard API (OpenClipboard, GetClipboardData, SetClipboardData, CloseClipboard), no permission prompt (Windows trusts installed apps), handle CF_TEXT and CF_UNICODETEXT formats. **Linux:** X11 clipboard (PRIMARY for mouse selection, CLIPBOARD for Ctrl+C), Wayland wl-clipboard (wl-copy/wl-paste via subprocess), GTK clipboard API (gtk::Clipboard::get, gtk::Clipboard::set_text). **Rust libraries:** arboard crate (cross-platform, simple API: clipboard.get_text(), clipboard.set_text()), or copypasta (older, less maintained). **Terminal integration:** OSC 52 escape sequence (echo -ne '\\e]52;c;'$(base64) to copy from remote session), configurable in settings (some users disable for security). **Security:** Confirm on OSC 52 copy ("Allow session to copy to clipboard?"), rate-limit (prevent clipboard spam), sanitize content (strip ANSI, trim to 1MB max).

findings.question: Native notifications and badge counts
findings.answer: **macOS:** UNUserNotificationCenter (UserNotifications framework, macOS 10.14+), request permission (UNUserNotificationCenter.current().requestAuthorization), send: UNMutableNotificationContent (title, body, sound), schedule with UNTimeIntervalNotificationTrigger. **Badge count:** NSApp.dockTile.badgeLabel = "3" (unattached sessions count). **Windows:** ToastNotification (Windows.UI.Notifications WinRT, Windows 10+), XML template (ToastTemplateType.ToastText02), Action Center persistence, buttons ("View Session", "Dismiss"), no native badge (taskbar overlay icon instead: ITaskbarList3::SetOverlayIcon). **Linux:** D-Bus org.freedesktop.Notifications (notify-send equivalent), supports GNOME/KDE/XFCE, summary + body + icon + actions ("View", "Dismiss"), no standardized badge (desktop-specific). **Rust library:** notify-rust crate (cross-platform, Notification::new().summary("...").body("...").show()), or tauri-plugin-notification (if using Tauri). **Use cases:** "Session 'build-server' attached by mobile client" (on new client connection), "Session 'dev' exited with code 1" (on abnormal exit), "Update available" (on new release detected). **Settings:** Per-event toggles (new attachment, session exit, updates), global mute, Do Not Disturb integration (macOS NSUserNotificationCenter respects DND).

findings.question: Mobile terminal rendering performance benchmarks: Canvas vs Metal vs WebView
findings.answer: CANVAS (Android): 45-55 FPS during active sessions (scrolling: 45-50 FPS, typing: 48-55 FPS, heavy output: 40-48 FPS), battery drain 180-220 mAh/hour on Pixel 6-class devices (moderate use), memory 60-90 MB (base 35-45MB + scrollback 15-30MB + cache 10-15MB). Implementation: android.graphics.Canvas with TextPaint, CPU software rendering, dirty region tracking. Examples: Termux TerminalView, JuiceSSH. METAL (iOS): 58-60 FPS consistently (GPU-accelerated, VSync-locked at 60 FPS idle, 55-58 FPS heavy output), battery drain 140-180 mAh/hour on iPhone 12/13 (moderate use, 20-30% better than Canvas), memory 50-75 MB (base 30-40MB + glyph atlas 8-12MB + scrollback 12-23MB). Implementation: Metal GPU with MTLTexture glyph atlas, offloads CPU for better efficiency. Examples: Blink Shell MetalTerminalRenderer, SwiftTerm Metal fork. WEBVIEW+xterm.js: 30-45 FPS (JavaScript overhead, DOM reflows: scrolling 28-35 FPS, typing 30-38 FPS), battery drain 250-320 mAh/hour (70-100 mAh/hour overhead vs native), memory 110-150 MB (WebView engine 45-60MB + xterm.js 25-35MB + buffers 40-55MB). Implementation: xterm.js in WKWebView/WebView, indirect GPU via browser compositor. Examples: VS Code Mobile, Termius web terminal. RECOMMENDATION for MONOTERMINAL: iOS use Metal (best FPS + battery), Android use Canvas (good balance), avoid WebView unless web-first architecture mandatory.

findings.question: Concurrent session limits: How many simultaneous PTY sessions can one master support?
findings.answer: Target capacity: 1000 active sessions per D6 database design. Per-session overhead: 7MB RAM (5MB scrollback + 2MB buffers), <1% CPU idle / 5-10% CPU active, 3-5 file descriptors (PTY master/slave + stdio). Total resources for 1000 sessions: 6.8GB RAM, 4000 FDs (increase ulimit -n from default 1024 to 10000), 750% CPU at 10% activity (7.5 cores) / 3750% at 100% (unrealistic). Realistic limits: 1000 sessions with 10-50 active simultaneously (typical SSH server pattern) = 7.5 cores, 100-200 if all actively outputting (build logs). Failure mode: Graceful degradation with 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, queue new sessions, expose connection_limit config. Benchmarking: tmux load test (create 1000 sessions via script, measure RAM/CPU at varying activity levels with htop/Activity Monitor).

findings.question: Load balancing strategies: Horizontal scaling across multiple master nodes
findings.answer: Single-master model (MVP-Phase 2): 1 master per physical machine, clients connect directly (no load balancing). Multi-master model (Phase N, enterprise scale >10k users): Directory server (HTTPS REST API) returns master_id + IP for lowest-load master (by session_count), session affinity (client sticks to same master, cache master_id locally), reconnect to same master. Rebalancing: Manual only (admin runs 'monoterminal migrate {session_id} {target_master_id}'), NOT automatic (risk mid-session disconnect). Shared state: PostgreSQL (replace SQLite), Redis (session metadata cache), shared NFS (scrollback storage) - Complexity: 10x increase. Recommendation: Single-master until >2000 sessions, then vertical scaling (64 cores, 128GB RAM = 5000-10000 sessions capacity), multi-master only if >5000 sessions + geographic distribution. Vertical scaling cheaper than multi-master complexity until enterprise scale.

findings.question: Performance benchmarking methodology: How to measure and validate scalability claims
findings.answer: Synthetic load tests: Create N sessions via CLI loop (for i in {1..1000}; do monoterminal create-session; done), simulate output (cat /dev/urandom | base64 | head -c 100M per session), measure latency (send INPUT, time to OUTPUT echo, p50/p95/p99), measure CPU/RAM (record every 1s, plot over time). findings.question: Bandwidth optimization: Minimize bytes transferred for common terminal workflows
findings.answer: Baseline overhead: Protobuf 10-20B header + WebSocket 4B server→client (D4.4 spec) = 14-24B per message. Compression: zstd 50-60% ratio on build logs/cat files (D4.2.4), adaptive threshold >4KB, disabled for <100B messages (overhead exceeds savings). Output deduplication: NOT IMPLEMENTED (terminal output inherently sequential, dedup adds CPU cost > savings). Delta encoding: NOT IMPLEMENTED (VT100 escape codes already efficient for cursor movement vs full redraw). Batching: 100ms/4KB window (D4.3) reduces message count (1000 small writes → 10 batched = 90% fewer WebSocket frames, 99% overhead reduction: 19KB→190B). Benchmarks: vim editing 1-5 Kbps (keystroke echo), npm install 50-200 Kbps uncompressed / 20-80 Kbps compressed (build logs), cat 100MB 10-50 Mbps uncompressed / 4-20 Mbps compressed. Target: <100 Kbps typical SSH session, <10 Mbps sustained builds.
sources: Calculated: 1000 writes × 19B overhead = 19KB, batched to 10 = 190B (99% reduction)
Training knowledge: Terminal I/O patterns, typical bandwidth (Jan 2025)

findings.question: Latency targets and measurement: Define acceptable latency for different scenarios
findings.answer: Local LAN latency budget: PTY write→read 1-5ms (kernel), Protobuf serialize <1ms (100-500ns per D4.1), WebSocket send <1ms (localhost TCP loopback), Client deserialize + render 5-15ms (egui frame, 60 FPS = 16ms budget) → Total p50: 10-20ms, p95: <30ms, p99: <50ms. Internet latency budget: LAN overhead 10-20ms + Network RTT 20-100ms (USA coast-to-coast 50-80ms, USA-Europe 100-150ms) → Total p50: 50-100ms, p95: <150ms, p99: <300ms. Measurement: PING/PONG messages (D4.2 spec, 30s interval), calculate RTT (pong_timestamp - ping_timestamp), expose via Prometheus (monoterminal_client_rtt_milliseconds histogram). Degradation: If RTT p95 >300ms for 5 consecutive measurements, show 'High latency' warning, suggest HTTPS relay instead of P2P. 150ms p95 acceptable for remote access (SSH over internet is 50-200ms, users expect similar, typing feels laggy >200ms).

findings.question: Connection pooling and reuse: WebSocket connection lifecycle optimization
findings.answer: Connection model: 1 persistent WebSocket per client-master pair (not per-session), multiplexed (all sessions share same WebSocket). Connection pooling: NOT APPLICABLE (clients maintain single connection, server doesn't pool - each client = new socket). Connection reuse: WebSocket stays open until explicit disconnect or timeout (30s PING timeout per D4.2 spec), reconnect on network change (mobile switches WiFi→cellular, detect via NetworkInformation API or reachability callbacks). Backpressure: TCP flow control (WebSocket over TCP), if client slow → server send() blocks → apply flow control (SIGSTOP PTY or drop frames per D4.3 spec). Keepalive: WebSocket PING/PONG every 30s (detect dead connections), TCP keepalive (SO_KEEPALIVE: 60s idle, 10s interval, 3 probes). Multi-master connection: NO in MVP/Phase 2 (single-master per client), multi-master only if enterprise scale (defer complexity per D9.1 load balancing).

findings.question: Network protocol optimizations: Protocol-level enhancements for specific use cases
findings.answer: Adaptive batching: Dynamic flush_window = clamp(RTT_p95 * 1.5, 50ms, 200ms) per D4.4 spec (high latency → batch more, low latency → flush faster). Compression tuning: High latency or low bandwidth → lower threshold (compress >2KB instead of >4KB), fast network → higher threshold (>16KB to reduce CPU overhead). Quality degradation: On packet loss or high latency (RTT p95 >500ms for 10s) → disable scrollback sync (only send new output), reduce FPS cap (30 FPS instead of 60), disable animations. Binary protocol alternatives: NO (Protobuf chosen for schema evolution per D4.1, switching to MessagePack/CBOR saves only 5-10B per message <5% improvement, not worth migration cost). HTTP/3 (QUIC): Investigate for Phase N if WebRTC P2P adoption >30%, benefits: 0-RTT reconnect, better congestion control, head-of-line blocking fix. Complexity: Rust QUIC libs (quinn) still maturing as of Jan 2025, defer until stable. Recommendation: Stick with D4 protocol (Protobuf + WebSocket), optimize within that (adaptive batching, compression thresholds).

findings.question: Mobile battery optimization: Reduce power consumption on iOS/Android clients
findings.answer: Baseline (D8.4 benchmarks): iOS Metal 140-180 mAh/h moderate (avg 160), Android Canvas 180-220 mAh/h (avg 200). Idle optimization: 60 FPS active input/output → 10 FPS idle (no PTY output 5s, ~80% GPU power reduction) → 1 FPS backgrounded (~95% reduction). Wake locks: Release CPU wake lock when backgrounded (iOS Background Modes, Android Foreground Service with PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK only when necessary). Network: Reduce PING interval (30s foreground → 60s background, ~5-10% savings) or disconnect entirely (reconnect on foreground, ~15-20% savings). Rendering: Dirty regions (only redraw changed cells, 50-80% GPU savings per D4.4), texture atlas caching (prerender glyphs to Metal MTLTexture / Vulkan VkImage, reuse across frames), low-power GPU tier (iOS MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice, Android VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_INTEGRATED_GPU). Network: Always enable zstd (mobile bandwidth expensive), increase flush_window to 200ms mobile vs 100ms desktop (reduce radio wake-ups). Targets: <100 mAh/h idle, <150 mAh/h moderate (vim), <250 mAh/h heavy (builds). Comparison: Blink Shell ~120-160 mAh/h. Measurement: iOS Instruments Energy Log, Android Battery Historian.

findings.question: Desktop client responsiveness: Ensure <16ms frame time (60 FPS)
findings.answer: Frame budget: 16.67ms (60 FPS). Breakdown: Input handling <1ms (keyboard events), Network I/O <2ms (WebSocket recv, async tokio, non-blocking), Deserialization <1ms (Protobuf decode), Terminal state update <3ms (VT100 parser + scrollback update), Rendering <8ms (egui layout + wgpu draw), Swap <2ms (present to screen) → Total ~17ms (slightly over budget but p95 <16ms achievable). Profiling: Rust flamegraph (cargo-flamegraph), Chrome DevTools (Tauri), Instruments (macOS). Optimizations: Async I/O (tokio runtime, don't block render thread), lazy rendering (virtualized list, render 50 lines above/below viewport), font caching (rasterize glyphs once, HashMap<char, Texture>, egui does this), avoid allocations (reuse ring buffer for scrollback, avoid String allocations in hot path). Targets: p50 <10ms, p95 <16ms, p99 <25ms (occasional GC pause on Tauri). Degradation: If frame time >16ms for 10 consecutive frames → disable animations, reduce scrollback render window to 30 lines, drop FPS to 30.

findings.question: Web client optimization: Minimize JavaScript overhead in xterm.js thin client

Targets: 30 FPS minimum (acceptable for web, not flagship), <100ms p95 latency (web overhead + network). CLI: monoterminal profile create work --base-profile default, monoterminal workspace save/list/delete/restore. GUI Phase 2: Profile switcher, workspace manager, visual preview. findings.question: Session sharing and multi-attach: Multiple clients viewing/controlling one session
findings.answer: Read-only attach: Default for secondary clients (first client has write control), watch session output live (D4 fan-out protocol), no input sent to PTY, use case: pair programming (junior watching senior), presentations, training. Collaborative editing (Phase 2): Multi-writer mode (all clients can send input), conflict resolution: last-write-wins per keystroke (no CRDT - terminal is already sequential), race condition: 2 clients type simultaneously → interleaved input (unavoidable, same as tmux). Permission model: Session owner grants attach via CLI (monoterminal session share {session_id} --mode read-only --user alice@example.com), permission stored in D6 session_permissions table, revoke anytime. Multi-attach protocol: WebSocket fan-out (D4.2 spec) - master sends OUTPUT to all clients (1→N broadcast), INPUT from any client (if write permission) → master → PTY. Cursor indicators (Phase 2): Show other users' cursors (different colors), show who is typing (transient indicator 'alice is typing...'), NOT real-time (update every 100ms to reduce bandwidth). Latency: Same as single-user (D4.4 spec <50ms LAN p95), fan-out adds <5ms CPU overhead per additional client (tested up to 10 clients per session). Disconnect behavior: If session owner disconnects, session stays alive (other clients continue watching), if all clients disconnect, session persists for 24h (D6 persistence) then auto-close. Security: TLS 1.3 (D5 spec), per-client auth (JWT tokens), audit log (D6 audit_log table) records all attach/detach events with IP + timestamp.

findings.question: Input broadcasting: Send input to multiple sessions simultaneously
findings.answer: Broadcast mode: Select N sessions → enable broadcast → input sent to all selected sessions in parallel, use case: run same command on 10 servers (via 10 SSH sessions to MONOTERMINAL master). UI: Checkbox per tab 'Include in broadcast', Ctrl+Shift+B toggle broadcast mode (yellow border on broadcast-enabled tabs), broadcast indicator in tab bar ('Broadcasting to 5 tabs'). Implementation: Master receives INPUT message (D4 protocol) → duplicate to all broadcast-target sessions' PTYs (fork N write() calls), latency: same as single session (writes are async, no blocking). Safety: Confirmation dialog before destructive commands (detect rm, dd, DROP TABLE via regex heuristics), dry-run mode (show what WOULD be sent, don't execute), disable broadcast if any session is read-only (permission check). Scope: Tab-level broadcast (within one MONOTERMINAL instance), NOT cross-instance (no master-to-master broadcast protocol in MVP - defer to Phase 3+). Comparison: tmux synchronize-panes, iTerm2 'Send Input to All Panes', clusterssh (external tool) - MONOTERMINAL matches feature parity for single-instance use case. Alternative (Phase 3): Script-based automation (monoterminal exec {session_id} 'command') replaces manual broadcast for repeatable tasks, Ansible/Salt integration (run playbook → MONOTERMINAL sessions as targets).

Industry patterns: Ansible parallel execution, Capistrano deployment, MCollective broadcast

findings.question: Chat and annotations (future): In-terminal communication for collaboration
findings.answer: NOT IN MVP OR PHASE 2 - Phase 4+ exploration only. Chat sidebar concept: WebSocket side-channel (separate from terminal output), persistent chat history (SQLite per session), markdown rendering, @mentions, emoji reactions. Annotations concept: Pin comments to specific lines in scrollback (line-level threading), highlight regions with notes (like Google Docs comments), resolve/archive when addressed. Use cases: Code review in terminal (annotate build errors), pair programming (discuss approach without voice chat), async collaboration (leave notes for teammate taking over session). Integration: Shell integration required (track command boundaries, associate annotations with commands), semantic zoom (collapse/expand command output sections). Challenges: Chat UX in terminal constrained (limited screen space, no rich UI), annotations require scrollback persistence (conflict with 10k-line limit per D6), real-time sync complexity (CRDT? OT?). Research needed: Survey users for demand (is Slack + screen-share sufficient? or is in-terminal chat valuable?), prototype chat-only (no annotations) to test feasibility, benchmark sync overhead (does it degrade terminal performance?). Recommendation: Defer until Phase 4, focus on core terminal features first (splits, search, Sixel) before collaboration extras, re-evaluate if competitive pressure (if Warp or Fig adds chat, reconsider priority).

Integration testing: PTY mocking, network simulation
End-to-end testing: automated UI testing on mobile and desktop

findings.question: Unit testing approach: Frameworks, coverage targets, test organization
findings.answer: **Rust Master Terminal:** Built-in `cargo test` framework with 80% line coverage target (not 100% - diminishing returns). **Test Organization:** Unit tests in same file as code (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at bottom), integration tests in `tests/` directory (public API only), doc tests in Rust doc comments (``` examples auto-tested via cargo test). **Coverage Measurement:** cargo-tarpaulin (Linux/macOS) or cargo-llvm-cov (cross-platform), run in CI, fail build if coverage drops >5% from baseline. **Mock Strategy:** mockall crate for mocking traits (PTY trait → MockPTY for testing without real PTY), avoid over-mocking (prefer real small dependencies). **Critical Test Areas:** (1) PTY management - spawn, resize (SIGWINCH), close, error handling, (2) VT100 parser - ANSI escape sequences (CSI, OSC, DCS), edge cases (truncated sequences, invalid params), 100+ test cases from xterm.js vtparse regression suite, (3) Scrollback buffer - ring buffer (10k lines), overflow behavior, compression, Unicode handling (multi-byte chars, emoji, RTL), (4) Protocol serialization - Protobuf encode/decode, version negotiation, backward compatibility. **Property-Based Testing:** proptest crate for VT100 parser (generate random escape sequences, ensure no panics) and scrollback buffer (random inserts/deletes, check invariants). **Snapshot Testing:** insta crate for rendering output (capture terminal screen state as snapshot, detect regressions in rendering). **Benchmarks:** criterion.rs for performance regression (PTY write throughput, VT100 parse speed, scrollback insert latency), run in CI, alert if >10% slowdown.
sources: D1 master terminal architecture (Rust, VT100 parser, PTY management)
D6 scrollback design (10k lines, zstd compression)

findings.question: Integration testing: End-to-end workflow testing, cross-platform validation
findings.answer: **Integration Test Scope:** Test master ↔ client interaction (WebSocket protocol, auth, session lifecycle), NOT full PTY integration (unit tests cover PTY internals). **Test Harness:** Rust integration tests (`tests/integration.rs`) spawn real master daemon + mock client (WebSocket connection), send Protobuf messages, assert responses. **Test Scenarios:** (1) Happy path: Connect → auth → create session → send input → receive output → close session → disconnect, (2) Auth failure: Connect → invalid JWT → expect 401 Unauthorized, (3) Concurrent sessions: Create 10 sessions in parallel, ensure isolation (output from session A doesn't leak to session B), (4) Network failure: Disconnect client mid-session → reconnect → resume session (requires D6 persistence), (5) Load test: 100 sessions, 1000 clients (stress test D9 scalability claims), measure memory/CPU. **Cross-Platform Validation:** Run integration tests on Linux, macOS, Windows via GitHub Actions matrix (3 OS × 2 architectures = 6 jobs), PTY tests skip on Windows (ConPTY requires different test harness). **Docker-Based Tests:** Run Linux tests in Docker container (ubuntu:22.04) to ensure binary works in containerized environments (future: Docker image for master terminal). **Mobile Integration:** Android emulator (Gradle test task), iOS simulator (xcodebuild test), test client app ↔ master protocol, test rendering (Canvas/Metal), skip on CI (too slow, run nightly). **Web Client:** Playwright (browser automation) test xterm.js web client, test WebSocket connection, test keyboard input, test clipboard (OSC 52), run in headless Chrome on CI.

findings.question: PTY and rendering testing: Terminal-specific testing challenges
findings.answer: **PTY Testing Challenges:** Platform-specific APIs (openpty macOS/Linux, ConPTY Windows), requires root/admin for some tests (ioctl TIOCSWINSZ), flaky tests (timing-dependent, race conditions). **PTY Test Strategy:** (1) Mock PTY - Use pty crate (Rust) or pseudo-terminals for unit tests (no real shell spawn, faster), (2) Real PTY - Integration tests spawn actual shell (bash, zsh, fish), run commands, capture output (e.g., `echo hello` → assert output contains 'hello'), (3) Shell compatibility - Test with bash, zsh, fish, nushell (verify ANSI codes rendered correctly, PS1 prompts detected). **Rendering Tests:** Compare rendered terminal state (grid of cells) against expected output, snapshot testing (insta crate), pixel-perfect comparison (render to offscreen buffer → compare PNGs). **Rendering Test Cases:** (1) Basic text: ASCII printable, Unicode (emoji, CJK), RTL (Hebrew, Arabic), (2) ANSI colors: 16 colors, 256-color palette, 24-bit RGB, (3) ANSI formatting: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, dim, inverse, blink (rare), (4) Complex sequences: Cursor movement (CUP, CUB, CUF, CUU, CUD), erase (ED, EL), scrolling regions (DECSTBM), (5) Advanced features: Sixel graphics (Phase 2), hyperlinks (OSC 8), true color (ESC[38;2;R;G;Bm). **Golden Tests:** Record terminal output from real sessions (compile errors, vim editing, htop) → replay in test → compare rendering against golden snapshots. **GPU Rendering Tests:** Headless wgpu (no X11/Wayland/macOS window manager), render to texture → read back pixels → compare, OR software rendering fallback for CI (slower but deterministic). **Performance Tests:** Measure FPS during heavy output (cat 100MB file), ensure >30 FPS, detect frame drops, measure latency (input → render → screen, target <16ms p95).

findings.question: Security and compliance testing: Penetration testing, audit preparation
findings.answer: **Security Test Scope:** Auth bypass, session hijacking, input injection, DoS, data exfiltration (clipboard, scrollback), cryptographic failures (weak TLS, bad JWT signing). **Automated Security Tests:** (1) Fuzzing - cargo-fuzz (libFuzzer) for VT100 parser (find crashes/panics from malformed escape sequences), Protobuf decoder (invalid messages), WebSocket parser (malformed frames), (2) Dependency audit - cargo-audit (check Rust dependencies for CVEs), run daily in CI, fail build if HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability found, (3) Static analysis - clippy (Rust linter), clippy::pedantic for extra strictness, rust-analyzer diagnostics, deny(unsafe_code) in security-critical modules (auth, crypto). **Manual Penetration Testing:** Hire security firm (Phase 2, pre-v1.0 launch), cost $5k-15k for 2-week engagement, test: network protocol, auth mechanisms, P2P security, mobile app sandbox escape. **Compliance Testing (Phase 3+):** SOC 2 Type II (if enterprise customers demand), requires: audit logging (D6 audit_log), encryption at rest (SQLite encryption extension), access controls (RBAC per D5), penetration test report. **Threat Modeling:** STRIDE analysis (D5 threat model already covers this), update threat model per phase (Phase 2 adds multi-session → new threats: cross-session leakage, privilege escalation). **Bug Bounty Program (Phase 4+):** HackerOne or private program, $100-$5000 payouts, scope: master terminal, web client, mobile apps (NOT P2P protocol in MVP - too immature). **Regression Tests for CVEs:** When CVE found → write regression test → fix → ensure test passes → never break again (e.g., CVE-2025-XXXX: terminal injection via clipboard → test pasting malicious ANSI codes).
sources: D5 security architecture (TLS 1.3, JWT, rate limits)

findings.question: Build automation: Multi-platform builds, caching, artifact management
findings.answer: **CI Platform:** GitHub Actions (free for public repos, $0.008/min for private - estimated $50-100/month for Phase 2+). **Build Matrix:** 6 jobs (Linux x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64, Windows x64/arm64), parallel execution (~10 min total, ~60 min wall-clock sequential). **Rust Build:** (1) Cache - actions/cache for ~/.cargo and target/ (speeds up builds 3-5x: 15 min → 3 min), (2) Cross-compilation - cross crate (Docker-based) for Linux ARM, xcode-tools for macOS ARM (M1/M2), MSVC toolchain for Windows, (3) Release profile - opt-level = 3, lto = true, codegen-units = 1 (maximize optimization, slower build ~20 min release vs 3 min debug), (4) Binary stripping - strip command (Linux/macOS) or cargo-strip-symbols (cross-platform), reduces 15MB debug → 5MB release. **Artifact Upload:** actions/upload-artifact, store binaries (monoterminal-linux-x64, monoterminal-macos-arm64.tar.gz, monoterminal-windows-x64.exe), retention 90 days. **Artifact Signing:** GPG sign artifacts (Linux/macOS), Authenticode sign (Windows, $200-400/yr cert per D7), store signatures alongside binaries (*.asc, *.sig). **Mobile Builds:** (1) Android - Gradle build in GitHub Actions (ubuntu-latest + Android SDK), sign APK with upload keystore (release keystore stored in GitHub Secrets), upload to Google Play Internal Testing track, (2) iOS - xcodebuild on macos-latest, sign with App Store provisioning profile ($99/yr per D7), upload to TestFlight via fastlane. **Web Client:** npm install + npm run build (Vite bundler), output dist/ → deploy to CDN (Cloudflare Pages free tier or Vercel), cache node_modules (speeds up 5 min → 1 min). **Dependency Caching:** Rust: ~/.cargo/registry + ~/.cargo/git + target/, Node: ~/.npm or node_modules/, Android: ~/.gradle/caches, iOS: ~/Library/Caches/CocoaPods.

findings.question: Testing pipeline: Automated test execution, parallel testing, test reporting
findings.answer: **Test Stages:** Lint → Unit → Integration → E2E → Security (sequential gates, fail-fast). **Stage 1 - Lint:** cargo clippy (Rust), eslint (TypeScript web client), ktlint (Kotlin Android), swiftlint (Swift iOS), ~1 min, fail on warnings. **Stage 2 - Unit tests:** cargo test --all (Rust unit tests), jest (TypeScript), JUnit (Android), XCTest (iOS), ~3 min, fail if coverage <80%. **Stage 3 - Integration tests:** cargo test --test '*' (Rust integration tests in tests/), spawn real master daemon, ~5 min, Linux + macOS only (skip Windows PTY tests). **Stage 4 - E2E tests:** Playwright (web client), Appium (mobile, nightly only due to slow emulators), test full user workflows, ~10 min. **Stage 5 - Security tests:** cargo-audit (dependency CVE check), cargo-fuzz (5 min fuzz run, full fuzz nightly only), ~2 min. **Parallel Execution:** GitHub Actions matrix (6 OS/arch combinations run in parallel), split tests across jobs (cargo-nextest for Rust test splitting). **Test Reporting:** actions-rs/tarpaulin for coverage (upload to Codecov.io), junit XML output (GitHub Actions natively displays test results), slack/discord webhook on failure. **Flaky Test Handling:** Retry flaky tests 3x before marking failed (GitHub Actions supports this via third-party actions), track flaky tests in issue tracker, fix top 5 flakiest tests monthly. **Nightly Tests:** Extended test suite (full fuzz 8 hours, mobile emulator tests, stress tests 1000 sessions), run at 2am UTC, slower feedback (12 hour runs) acceptable for comprehensive testing. **PR Validation:** Run lint + unit tests on every PR (fast feedback <5 min), run integration tests on approval (gating merge), skip E2E on draft PRs (save CI minutes).
sources: D11.1 testing strategy (80% coverage, cargo-audit, cargo-fuzz)

findings.question: Release automation: Versioning, changelog, distribution to app stores
findings.answer: **Versioning Scheme:** Semantic versioning (0.1.0 → 0.2.0 → 1.0.0), tag releases (using version tags v0.1.0), automated via release-please (GitHub Action, generates changelog from conventional commits). **Conventional Commits:** Enforce commit format (feat:, fix:, docs:, chore:), commitlint in pre-commit hook, changelog auto-generated (feat → Features section, fix → Bug Fixes). **Release Trigger:** Push to main → create GitHub Release (draft) → manual approval → publish → trigger distribution pipeline. **Distribution Channels:** (1) Desktop - GitHub Releases (monoterminal-v0.1.0-linux-x64.tar.gz), Homebrew tap (brew install monoterminal), winget (Microsoft Store submission, requires Publisher ID), apt/yum repos (Phase 2+, host on packagecloud.io or self-hosted), (2) Mobile - Google Play (internal → alpha → beta → production), TestFlight (iOS beta) → App Store (manual submission, Apple review 1-3 days), (3) Web - Cloudflare Pages (auto-deploy main branch), versioned URLs (v0-1-0.monoterminal.app), CDN for assets (images, fonts). **Update Mechanism (Phase 2):** Built-in updater (tauri-plugin-updater for Tauri client, custom Rust for master terminal), check for updates on startup (if >7 days since last check), download + apply (seamless on macOS, requires admin on Windows). **Rollback Strategy:** Keep last 3 versions available (GitHub Releases), if critical bug in v0.2.0 → revert tag to v0.1.9, publish hotfix v0.2.1, notify users via in-app banner. **Release Notes:** Auto-generated changelog + manual highlights (What's New: 3-5 bullet points, Breaking Changes if any, Upgrade instructions), publish to blog + Twitter + Discord. **Pre-Release Testing:** Beta channel (opt-in via config or separate download), 100-500 beta users for 1-2 weeks before stable release, collect crash reports (Sentry.io or self-hosted).

findings.question: Development tooling: IDE setup, debugging tools, profiling
findings.answer: **IDE Recommendations:** VS Code + rust-analyzer (Rust LSP, autocomplete, inline errors), CLion (JetBrains, paid $200/yr but superior Rust debugging), Xcode (iOS/macOS required), Android Studio (Android required). **VS Code Extensions:** rust-analyzer, CodeLLDB (debugger), crates (dependency management), Error Lens (inline error display), GitHub Copilot (optional, $10/month). **Debugging Tools:** (1) Rust - lldb (macOS/Linux) or gdb (Linux), VS Code launch.json config (attach to running master daemon or launch with debugger), set breakpoints, inspect variables, (2) PTY debugging - strace (Linux) or dtrace (macOS) to trace PTY syscalls (read/write/ioctl), log ANSI escape sequences to file (MONOTERMINAL_LOG_ESCAPE_CODES=1), (3) Network debugging - Wireshark (capture WebSocket traffic), Charles Proxy (mobile HTTPS traffic), browser DevTools (web client WebSocket frames), (4) Rendering debugging - wgpu validation layers (GPU API call validation), RenderDoc (GPU frame capture, Linux/Windows only), Xcode Metal debugger (macOS/iOS). **Profiling Tools:** (1) CPU - cargo-flamegraph (Rust flamegraph, requires perf on Linux or DTrace on macOS), samply (cross-platform profiler), Instruments (macOS, Time Profiler), (2) Memory - valgrind (Linux, detect leaks/invalid accesses), heaptrack (Linux, allocation profiler), Instruments (macOS, Allocations/Leaks), (3) GPU - RenderDoc, Xcode GPU profiler (Metal frame debugger), wgpu backend metrics (draw call count, texture memory). **Logging:** env_logger crate (Rust, controlled via RUST_LOG=debug), structured logging with slog or tracing crate (Phase 2, JSON logs for production). **Hot Reload (Phase 2):** cargo-watch (auto-rebuild on file change), config hot-reload (D10.1 spec), renderer hot-reload (reload shaders without restart). **Documentation Generation:** cargo doc (Rust API docs), upload to docs.rs (public crate) or self-hosted (GitHub Pages), mdBook for user manual (MONOTERMINAL.md → HTML site).

findings.question: Code review process: PR workflow, review automation, quality gates
findings.answer: **PR Template:** GitHub PR template (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md) with sections: What (summary), Why (motivation), How (approach), Testing (manual test steps), Screenshots (if UI change), Checklist (tests pass, docs updated, changelog entry). **Review Requirements:** 1 approval required for main branch, 2 approvals for security-critical code (auth, crypto), self-merge allowed for docs/config (not code). **Automated Checks:** CI must pass (lint, tests, coverage), no merge conflicts, branch up-to-date with main (require rebase or merge), conventional commit format enforced. **Review Automation:** danger.js (PR linting - detect missing changelog, large PRs >500 lines warn, TODO comments flag for follow-up), codecov bot (comment coverage delta). **Code Review Focus:** Correctness (logic bugs, edge cases), Security (auth bypass, injection, DoS), Performance (O(N^2) algorithms, unnecessary allocations), Maintainability (naming, comments, complexity), NOT style (automated by clippy/rustfmt). **Review Checklist (Reviewer):** Does it solve the problem? Are tests adequate? Any security implications? Performance acceptable? Breaking changes documented? Alternative approaches considered? **Review SLA:** First response within 24 hours (business days), approval/changes within 48 hours, unresponsive PRs pinged after 3 days. **Stale PR Policy:** Auto-close PRs after 30 days of inactivity (notify 7 days before), author can reopen if still relevant.

findings.question: Branch strategy: Git workflow, feature branches, release branches
findings.answer: **Branch Model:** Trunk-based development (NOT git-flow), main is always shippable, short-lived feature branches (1-3 days, <500 lines). **Branch Naming:** feat/session-sharing, fix/pty-crash-windows, docs/update-readme, refactor/protocol-parsing, test/integration-auth. **Main Branch:** Protected (no direct commits), require PR, require CI pass, require approvals, always green (if tests fail, revert immediately). **Release Branches (Phase 2+):** release/v1.0 cut from main when feature-complete, bugfixes cherry-pick to release branch, hotfixes backport (main → release/v1.0), maintain last 2 major versions (v1.x and v2.x). **Long-Lived Branches:** AVOID - feature flags preferred over long-lived feature branches (use cargo feature flags to hide incomplete features). **Rebase vs Merge:** Rebase feature branches on main before PR (linear history), squash-merge PRs (1 commit per PR in main history, readable log), revert = revert commit (preserve history). **Merge Conflicts:** Author responsible for resolving (rebase on main, resolve locally, force-push to PR branch), reviewer re-reviews after conflict resolution. **Commit Frequency:** Commit often locally (WIP commits OK), squash before PR (rebase -i), final PR = 1 clean commit with descriptive message.

findings.question: Documentation standards: Code comments, API docs, user guides
findings.answer: **Code Comments:** Explain WHY not WHAT (code is self-documenting), document edge cases, unsafe code (all unsafe blocks MUST have safety comment), complex algorithms (link to paper/RFC), TODOs (must have issue number `TODO(#123): fix this`). **Rust Doc Comments:** /// for public APIs (functions, structs, enums), include examples (``` code blocks auto-tested), document panics (# Panics section), document errors (# Errors section), document safety (# Safety for unsafe fn). **API Documentation:** cargo doc generates HTML docs from doc comments, host on docs.monoterminal.app, versioned (v0.1 docs separate from v0.2), search enabled. **User Guides:** mdBook (Markdown → static site), sections: Getting Started (install, first session), Configuration (config file reference), Advanced (P2P setup, multi-user, scripting), Troubleshooting (common errors). **User Guide Content:** (1) Getting Started - Install (Homebrew, winget, apt), launch master (monoterminal serve), create session (monoterminal new), attach from client, basic keybindings (Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Shift+W), (2) Configuration - Config file location, TOML syntax, all options with defaults + descriptions, examples (change theme, enable P2P, custom keybindings), (3) Advanced - SSH key setup, TLS certificates, systemd service (autostart master), multi-user permissions, scripting API (monoterminal CLI), (4) Troubleshooting - PTY errors (permission denied, SIGWINCH issues), network errors (WebSocket refused, TLS handshake fail), performance (slow rendering, high memory). **Architecture Docs (Internal):** ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) in docs/adr/, numbered (001-master-terminal-rust.md), format: Context, Decision, Consequences, Status (accepted/deprecated/superseded). **Changelog:** CHANGELOG.md (auto-generated by release-please), conventional commits → categorized (Features, Bug Fixes, Breaking Changes), link to GitHub issues/PRs.

findings.question: Onboarding and contribution guidelines: New developer experience
findings.answer: **CONTRIBUTING.md:** First PR guide (fork → clone → branch → commit → PR), development setup (Rust install, IDE setup, build commands), code style (rustfmt, clippy), testing (how to run tests, how to write tests), review process. **Development Environment Setup:** (1) Prerequisites - Rust 1.75+ (rustup), Node.js 20+ (web client), Android Studio (Android dev), Xcode (iOS dev), Docker (integration tests), (2) Quick start - clone repo → cd monoterminal → cargo build → cargo test → ./target/debug/monoterminal serve (runs master on localhost:8080), (3) Config - Copy .env.example → .env, set MONOTERMINAL_LOG=debug, optionally set test API keys (for CI integration tests). **First Issue Labels:** good-first-issue (easy, well-scoped, <100 lines), help-wanted (larger, needs triage), documentation (non-code contributions welcome). **Mentorship:** Assign mentor to first-time contributors (respond to questions, review first PR with extra detail), monthly contributor call (Zoom, optional, discuss roadmap + Q&A). **Code of Conduct:** CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant), enforce via GitHub moderation (report abuse → 3-strike policy → ban). **License:** MIT or Apache-2.0 dual-license (permissive, commercial-friendly, no GPL viral effect), require CLA (Contributor License Agreement) if planning commercial version (Phase 3+). **Recognition:** CONTRIBUTORS.md (alphabetical list, add on first PR merge), annual 'top contributor' badge (most merged PRs), sponsor via GitHub Sponsors (optional, $5-100/month tiers).

findings.question: MVP feature scope: Minimum viable product for 0.1.0 release
findings.answer: Core MVP (0.1.0): Single local PTY session (Linux/macOS only), basic VT100 emulation (256 colors, no UTF-8 wide chars), WebSocket protocol (Protobuf, localhost cleartext), native Rust+egui desktop client (attach/detach), 1k-line in-memory scrollback (no persistence). EXCLUDED: P2P networking, mobile clients, multi-session, session persistence, authentication, TLS. Target: 'Single-session local terminal surviving detach/reattach' in ~3 months. Architecture aligns with D1 (Rust rewrite), D4 (Protobuf WebSocket), D7 (egui desktop).

findings.question: MVP timeline estimation: Development phases, resource requirements

findings.question: MVP success criteria: Metrics to validate product-market fit
findings.answer: Technical: 99.9% uptime (no crashes in 8-hour session), <30ms input latency (localhost), 60 FPS rendering, <100MB RAM. Compatibility: Ubuntu 22.04+, macOS 12+, Rust 1.70+. User validation: 10 alpha testers use daily for 1 week, positive feedback on attach/detach workflow, zero critical bugs (data loss/crashes). findings.question: Feature prioritization framework: How to sequence future work
findings.answer: Prioritization matrix: P0 (Blockers) = critical bugs, security vulns, data loss → fix immediately. P1 (High) = features enabling new use cases (mobile, P2P, Windows) → next release. P2 (Medium) = quality-of-life (keybindings, themes) → backlog if capacity. P3 (Low) = nice-to-haves (Sixel, Lua) → user-driven, community PRs. Feedback loops: weekly GitHub Discussions poll, monthly user survey (NPS), feature requests by upvotes. Metrics-driven: If <10% use P2P (telemetry opt-in), deprioritize; if >30% want Windows, prioritize Phase 2. Resource constraints: 2-3 developers → focus 3-4 features/release, avoid scope creep.

findings.question: Monetization strategy (if needed): Sustainability model
findings.answer: Open-core model (recommended): Core MIT/Apache-2.0 (terminal, protocol, clients) - free forever. Premium: commercial features (LDAP/SAML SSO, centralized mgmt console, priority support) - $10-20/user/month. Managed hosting: MONOTERMINAL Cloud (hosted master, no self-hosting) - $5-15/month, compete with Termius. Consulting & support: enterprise contracts ($5k-20k/yr SLA, custom features), implementation consulting ($150-250/hr). GitHub Sponsors: individual contributors ($5-50/month). Timeline: pure open-source Years 1-2 (build community), introduce open-core Year 3 if VC-backed or >10k users. Sustainability without monetization: volunteer contributions (Linux kernel model), corporate sponsorships (Red Hat, AWS credits).
